by: product-os-keeper, for #1021 (reorganise the business intents): BI-4 (Code → Validation) close
source: The product owner's approval of 2026-11-10, reply "yes, apply and commit and cp", recorded in .garura/project/issues/1021/context/bi-4-close/approval.md, of the proposal in .garura/project/issues/1021/context/bi-4-close/proposal.md: BI-4's Outcome, Proof it is met and Must not; the domain page's last sentence; the 22 quotes of BI-4's Must not; "Validate its own code" on 2 BI-3 lines with its quotes; the testing owners on 5 BI-2 lines with their quotes.

changes.old: This domain turns a business intent into working code that a check from the outside can prove. It serves the product owner, who names the work, the technical lead, who designs it, and the developer, who builds it. It specifies the product, sets the project's design, and builds the work test first. It writes the eval that says if the work is met before the work is built, and it never gives a builder the eval or the tests: a check flags each build session that read them. It does not run the evals, release the work, or run the product.
changes.new: This domain turns a business intent into working code that a check from the outside can prove. It serves the product owner, who names the work, the technical lead, who designs it, and the developer, who builds it. It specifies the product, sets the project's design, and builds the work test first. It writes the eval that says if the work is met before the work is built, and it never gives a builder the eval or the tests: a check flags each build session that read them. It then tests the built work from outside the builder, by its evals and against the levels, surfaces, designs and standards set before the build. It does not release the work or run the product.

changes.old: - Out: writing and running the tests. The testing capabilities of Validation → Run (security, automated functional, performance, other testing and user acceptance testing) and Test with evals the builder never sees (Code → Validation) own the tests, and Design for evaluation and testing designs each slice's eval. This capability says which tests run in which environment and what a change must pass to move on.

This capability says which tests run in which environment and what a change must pass to move on.

changes.old: The code here is what a project keeps in its repository and builds from: the code it runs, its tests and its settings, and the documents, decision records, product model pages and memory written with them. For a coding agent's harness, the plays, skills and agents that tell a coding agent how to work, such as Garura, those are its code. A change is one piece of work raised for review and merged on its own, such as a pull request on GitHub. A standard is what the project decided its code must keep to, before the change was made: the review's rules for each kind of work, the project's own coding standards, the architecture with its technology and the design of the work in force, and the product profile's maintainability and reliability levels. The product profile is the record of the product's shape and the quality levels it commits to, each with a pass bar, the standard or measure that says when the product meets that level. In the product owner's words, Code → Validation "is about testing", and the list he approved renamed "Validate its own code" to this name, "because the old name read like the builder grading itself, which BI-4's Must not forbids." changes.old: **Outcome:** Code is proven to do what the spec asked, by evals its builder never sees, and every change lands the same way.
changes.new: **Outcome:** Built code is proven from outside before it moves on: what the product does is tested by evals its builder never sees; its security, performance, accessibility and user experience on each surface are tested in the testing environment against the levels and designs set before the build; and every change and the whole built work are checked against the project's standards.

changes.old: - Every change lands reviewed, and a person approves the merge.
changes.new: - Every level the product profile sets, and each surface and screen design, has a pass, a fail or a reason it was not tested, from tests run in the testing environment, never in production.

changes.old: **Must not:** Let a builder grade itself, weaken a check to pass, or merge without a person.
changes.new: **Must not:** Let a builder grade itself, weaken a check to pass, or count a check that did not run as a pass.

changes.add: - Every change is checked against the project's standards, by a part that is not its builder, before it is merged.
